title: Two Sum
problem_statement: Given an array of integers 'nums' and an integer target 't', return the indices of the two numbers such that they add up to 't'. Assume exactly one solution exists, and you may not use the same element twice.
input_format: First line contains N and t. Second line contains N integers.
output_format: Print the two indices (0-based) whose values sum to t.

title: Find Missing Number
problem_statement: Given an array containing N distinct numbers taken from 0 to N, find the one number that is missing from the array.
input_format: First line contains N. Second line contains N integers.
output_format: Print the missing number.

title: Contains Duplicate
problem_statement: Given an array of integers, determine if any value appears at least twice in the array.
input_format: First line contains N. Second line contains N integers.
output_format: Print 'true' if any duplicate exists, otherwise 'false'.

title: Remove Duplicates from Sorted Array
problem_statement: Given a sorted array, remove the duplicates in-place such that each unique element appears only once, and return the new length.
input_format: First line contains N. Second line contains N sorted integers.
output_format: Print the new length followed by the modified array.

title: Move Zeroes
problem_statement: Given an array of integers, move all zeroes to the end while maintaining the relative order of the non-zero elements.
input_format: First line contains N. Second line contains N integers.
output_format: Print the array after moving all zeroes to the end.

title: Best Time to Buy and Sell Stock
problem_statement: Given an array of prices where prices[i] is the price of a stock on day i, find the maximum profit achievable by buying on one day and selling on a later day.
input_format: First line contains N. Second line contains N integers representing prices.
output_format: Print the maximum profit possible. Print 0 if no profit is possible.

title: Maximum Subarray
problem_statement: Given an integer array, find the contiguous subarray (containing at least one number) which has the largest sum, and return that sum.
input_format: First line contains N. Second line contains N integers.
output_format: Print the maximum subarray sum.

title: Product of Array Except Self
problem_statement: Given an array of N integers, return an array where each element at index i is the product of all elements except nums[i], without using division.
input_format: First line contains N. Second line contains N integers.
output_format: Print the resulting array.

title: Rotate Array
problem_statement: Given an array, rotate the array to the right by k steps, where k is non-negative.
input_format: First line contains N and k. Second line contains N integers.
output_format: Print the array after rotating right by k steps.

title: Merge Sorted Arrays
problem_statement: Given two sorted arrays, merge them into a single sorted array.
input_format: First line contains M and N. Next two lines contain M and N sorted integers respectively.
output_format: Print the merged sorted array.

title: Majority Element
problem_statement: Given an array of size N, find the majority element - the element that appears more than N/2 times. Assume the majority element always exists.
input_format: First line contains N. Second line contains N integers.
output_format: Print the majority element.

title: Find Pivot Index
problem_statement: Given an array, find the leftmost pivot index where the sum of all numbers to the left equals the sum of all numbers to the right. Return -1 if no such index exists.
input_format: First line contains N. Second line contains N integers.
output_format: Print the pivot index, or -1 if it does not exist.

title: Third Maximum Number
problem_statement: Given an integer array, return the third distinct maximum number. If it does not exist, return the maximum number.
input_format: First line contains N. Second line contains N integers.
output_format: Print the third maximum, or the maximum if the third does not exist.

title: Missing Ranges
problem_statement: Given a sorted array of unique integers and a range [lower, upper], return the shortest sorted list of ranges that exactly covers all missing numbers.
input_format: First line contains N, lower, upper. Second line contains N sorted unique integers.
output_format: Print the missing ranges.

title: Sort Colors
problem_statement: Given an array with N objects colored red, white, or blue represented by 0, 1, and 2, sort them in-place so objects of the same color are adjacent, in the order 0, 1, 2 (Dutch National Flag problem).
input_format: First line contains N. Second line contains N integers (0, 1, or 2).
output_format: Print the sorted array.

title: Kth Largest Element
problem_statement: Given an unsorted array and an integer k, find the kth largest element in the array.
input_format: First line contains N and k. Second line contains N integers.
output_format: Print the kth largest element.

title: Find All Duplicates
problem_statement: Given an array of integers where 1 <= a[i] <= N (N = size of array), some elements appear twice and others once. Find all elements that appear twice.
input_format: First line contains N. Second line contains N integers.
output_format: Print all elements that appear twice.

title: Maximum Product Subarray
problem_statement: Given an integer array, find the contiguous subarray within the array that has the largest product, and return that product.
input_format: First line contains N. Second line contains N integers.
output_format: Print the maximum product of a contiguous subarray.

title: Longest Consecutive Sequence
problem_statement: Given an unsorted array of integers, find the length of the longest consecutive elements sequence, in O(n) time.
input_format: First line contains N. Second line contains N integers.
output_format: Print the length of the longest consecutive sequence.

title: Spiral Matrix
problem_statement: Given an m x n matrix, return all elements of the matrix in spiral order.
input_format: First line contains rows and cols. Following lines contain the matrix elements.
output_format: Print all elements in spiral order.

title: Set Matrix Zeroes
problem_statement: Given an m x n matrix, if an element is 0, set its entire row and column to 0. Do it in-place.
input_format: First line contains rows and cols. Following lines contain the matrix elements.
output_format: Print the modified matrix.

title: Rotate Matrix
problem_statement: Given an n x n 2D matrix, rotate the matrix by 90 degrees clockwise in-place.
input_format: First line contains n. Following n lines contain n integers each.
output_format: Print the rotated matrix.

title: Merge Intervals
problem_statement: Given an array of intervals, merge all overlapping intervals and return an array of the non-overlapping intervals covering all intervals in the input.
input_format: First line contains N (number of intervals). Next N lines contain start and end of each interval.
output_format: Print the merged intervals.

title: Insert Interval
problem_statement: Given a set of non-overlapping intervals sorted by start time, insert a new interval into the intervals, merging if necessary.
input_format: First line contains N. Next N lines contain intervals. Last line contains the new interval to insert.
output_format: Print the resulting list of intervals.

title: Summary Ranges
problem_statement: Given a sorted unique integer array, return the smallest sorted list of ranges that cover all numbers in the array exactly.
input_format: First line contains N. Second line contains N sorted unique integers.
output_format: Print the summary ranges.

title: Minimum Size Subarray Sum
problem_statement: Given an array of positive integers and a target sum, find the minimal length of a contiguous subarray of which the sum is greater than or equal to target. Return 0 if no such subarray exists.
input_format: First line contains N and target. Second line contains N integers.
output_format: Print the minimal length, or 0 if none exists.

title: Trapping Rain Water
problem_statement: Given N non-negative integers representing an elevation map where the width of each bar is 1, compute how much water it can trap after raining.
input_format: First line contains N. Second line contains N integers.
output_format: Print the total trapped water.

title: Container With Most Water
problem_statement: Given N non-negative integers representing heights of vertical lines, find two lines that together with the x-axis form a container that holds the most water.
input_format: First line contains N. Second line contains N integers.
output_format: Print the maximum amount of water the container can hold.

title: Candy Distribution
problem_statement: There are N children standing in a line, each with a rating value. Each child must get at least one candy, and children with a higher rating get more candies than their neighbors. Find the minimum number of candies needed.
input_format: First line contains N. Second line contains N integers representing ratings.
output_format: Print the minimum total number of candies required.

title: Gas Station
problem_statement: There are N gas stations along a circular route, with gas[i] amount of gas at station i and it costs cost[i] to travel from station i to station i+1. Find the starting gas station index from which you can travel around the circuit once, or -1 if not possible.
input_format: First line contains N. Second line contains gas array. Third line contains cost array.
output_format: Print the starting station index, or -1 if impossible.

title: Jump Game
problem_statement: Given an array of non-negative integers where each element represents the maximum jump length at that position, determine if you can reach the last index starting from the first index.
input_format: First line contains N. Second line contains N integers.
output_format: Print 'true' if the last index is reachable, otherwise 'false'.

title: Jump Game II
problem_statement: Given an array of non-negative integers where each element represents the maximum jump length at that position, find the minimum number of jumps required to reach the last index.
input_format: First line contains N. Second line contains N integers.
output_format: Print the minimum number of jumps needed.

title: Next Permutation
problem_statement: Given an array of integers representing a permutation, rearrange it into the lexicographically next greater permutation. If no such permutation exists, rearrange it as the lowest possible order (sorted ascending), in-place.
input_format: First line contains N. Second line contains N integers.
output_format: Print the next permutation.

title: Dutch National Flag
problem_statement: Given an array containing only 0s, 1s, and 2s, sort the array in a single pass using constant extra space (three-way partitioning around a pivot).
input_format: First line contains N. Second line contains N integers (0, 1, or 2).
output_format: Print the sorted array.

title: Rearrange Positive and Negative Numbers
problem_statement: Given an array of positive and negative integers, rearrange them so that positive and negative numbers are placed alternately, preserving the relative order where possible.
input_format: First line contains N. Second line contains N integers.
output_format: Print the rearranged array.

title: Maximum Circular Subarray
problem_statement: Given a circular integer array, find the maximum possible sum of a non-empty subarray, where the subarray may wrap around from the end to the beginning.
input_format: First line contains N. Second line contains N integers.
output_format: Print the maximum circular subarray sum.

title: Find Peak Element
problem_statement: Given an integer array, find a peak element (an element strictly greater than its neighbors) and return its index. If multiple peaks exist, return the index of any one of them.
input_format: First line contains N. Second line contains N integers.
output_format: Print the index of any peak element.

title: Missing Positive Number
problem_statement: Given an unsorted integer array, find the smallest missing positive integer, using O(n) time and O(1) extra space.
input_format: First line contains N. Second line contains N integers.
output_format: Print the smallest missing positive integer.

title: Rotate Image
problem_statement: Given an n x n 2D matrix representing an image, rotate the image by 90 degrees clockwise in-place.
input_format: First line contains n. Following n lines contain n integers each.
output_format: Print the rotated matrix.

title: Array Partition
problem_statement: Given an integer array of 2N numbers, group them into N pairs so that the sum of the minimum of each pair is maximized.
input_format: First line contains 2N. Second line contains 2N integers.
output_format: Print the maximized sum of minimums.

title: Two Sum using HashMap
problem_statement: Given an array of integers and a target, use a hashmap to find the indices of two numbers such that they add up to the target, in O(n) time.
input_format: First line contains N and target. Second line contains N integers.
output_format: Print the two indices whose values sum to the target.

title: Frequency Counter
problem_statement: Given an array of elements, build a frequency map counting how many times each distinct element appears.
input_format: First line contains N. Second line contains N integers.
output_format: Print each distinct element with its frequency.

title: Top K Frequent Elements
problem_statement: Given an integer array and an integer k, return the k most frequent elements in the array.
input_format: First line contains N and k. Second line contains N integers.
output_format: Print the k most frequent elements.

title: Happy Number
problem_statement: Given a number n, determine if it is a 'happy number', i.e., repeatedly replacing it with the sum of the squares of its digits eventually results in 1. Use a hashset to detect cycles.
input_format: A single line containing n.
output_format: Print 'true' if n is a happy number, otherwise 'false'.

title: Isomorphic Strings
problem_statement: Given two strings s and t, use two hashmaps to determine if they are isomorphic, meaning there exists a consistent character mapping between s and t.
input_format: First line contains s. Second line contains t.
output_format: Print 'true' if isomorphic, otherwise 'false'.

title: Group Shifted Strings
problem_statement: Given an array of strings, group all strings that belong to the same shifting sequence, where each letter is shifted by the same offset in a cyclic manner.
input_format: First line contains N. Second line contains N space separated strings.
output_format: Print the groups of shifted strings.

title: Subarray Sum Equals K
problem_statement: Given an array of integers and an integer k, use a prefix-sum hashmap to find the total number of continuous subarrays whose sum equals k.
input_format: First line contains N and k. Second line contains N integers.
output_format: Print the count of subarrays whose sum equals k.

title: Longest Harmonious Subsequence
problem_statement: Given an integer array, find the length of the longest subsequence where the difference between the maximum and minimum value is exactly 1.
input_format: First line contains N. Second line contains N integers.
output_format: Print the length of the longest harmonious subsequence.

title: Word Frequency
problem_statement: Given a paragraph of text, use a hashmap to count the frequency of each word and return the words sorted by decreasing frequency.
input_format: A single line containing the paragraph.
output_format: Print each word with its frequency, sorted by decreasing frequency.
example_input: the day is sunny the the the sunny is is

title: Count Distinct Elements
problem_statement: Given an array, count the number of distinct elements in every window of size k using a hashmap.
input_format: First line contains N and k. Second line contains N integers.
output_format: Print the count of distinct elements for each window.

title: Find Duplicate File
problem_statement: Given a list of directory paths with file names and content, group files with identical content together using a hashmap keyed by content.
input_format: First line contains N. Next N lines contain directory path followed by files and their content.
output_format: Print groups of file paths that have identical content.

title: Common Characters
problem_statement: Given an array of strings, find all characters that appear in all strings (including duplicates), using frequency hashmaps.
input_format: First line contains N. Second line contains N space separated strings.
output_format: Print the list of common characters.

title: First Unique Character
problem_statement: Given a string, find the index of the first non-repeating character using a hashmap. Return -1 if it does not exist.
input_format: A single line containing the string.
output_format: Print the index of the first unique character, or -1.

title: Majority Element II
problem_statement: Given an integer array of size n, find all elements that appear more than n/3 times, using a hashmap based counting approach.
input_format: First line contains N. Second line contains N integers.
output_format: Print all elements that appear more than n/3 times.

title: Longest Equal Subarray
problem_statement: Given a binary array, find the length of the longest contiguous subarray with an equal number of 0s and 1s, using a hashmap of prefix sums.
input_format: First line contains N. Second line contains N integers (0 or 1).
output_format: Print the length of the longest equal subarray.

title: Count Good Pairs
problem_statement: Given an array of integers, count the number of good pairs (i, j) where i < j and nums[i] == nums[j], using a frequency hashmap.
input_format: First line contains N. Second line contains N integers.
output_format: Print the number of good pairs.

title: Most Frequent Even Number
problem_statement: Given an integer array, use a hashmap to return the most frequent even element. If multiple elements are equally frequent, return the smallest one. Return -1 if no even element exists.
input_format: First line contains N. Second line contains N integers.
output_format: Print the most frequent even number, or -1.

title: Intersection of Arrays
problem_statement: Given two integer arrays, return their intersection such that each element appears as many times as it shows in both arrays, using a hashmap.
input_format: First line contains N and M. Second line contains N integers. Third line contains M integers.
output_format: Print the intersection array.

title: Find Difference of Arrays
problem_statement: Given two integer arrays, find the distinct elements present in the first array but not in the second, and vice versa, using hashsets.
input_format: First line contains N and M. Second line contains N integers. Third line contains M integers.
output_format: Print the two lists of distinct differences.

title: Pair Sum
problem_statement: Given an array and a target sum, use a hashmap to count all unique pairs of elements whose sum equals the target.
input_format: First line contains N and target. Second line contains N integers.
output_format: Print the count of unique pairs whose sum equals target.

title: Random Pick
problem_statement: Given an array of integers with possible duplicates and a target number, design a data structure that picks a random index of the target uniformly, using a hashmap of indices per value.
input_format: First line contains N. Second line contains N integers. Third line contains the target to pick.
output_format: Print any valid index at which the target occurs.

title: Design HashMap
problem_statement: Design a HashMap without using any built-in hash table libraries, supporting put(key, value), get(key), and remove(key) operations.
input_format: A sequence of operations: put, get, remove with their arguments.
output_format: Print the result of each get operation performed.
example_input:
put 1 1
put 2 2
get 1
get 3
put 2 1
get 2
remove 2
get 2

title: Design HashSet
problem_statement: Design a HashSet without using any built-in hash set libraries, supporting add(key), remove(key), and contains(key) operations.
input_format: A sequence of operations: add, remove, contains with their arguments.
output_format: Print the result of each contains operation performed.
example_input:
add 1
add 2
contains 1
contains 3
add 3
contains 3
remove 2
contains 2

title: Sparse Vector Dot Product
problem_statement: Given two sparse vectors represented as arrays, design a class using a hashmap to store only non-zero values, and implement an efficient dot product method.
input_format: First line contains N. Second and third lines contain the two vectors of size N.
output_format: Print the dot product of the two vectors.

title: LRU Cache
problem_statement: Design a Least Recently Used (LRU) cache with a fixed capacity that supports get(key) and put(key, value) in O(1) time, using a combination of a hashmap and a doubly linked list.
input_format: First line contains the capacity. Following lines contain operations: get or put with their arguments.
output_format: Print the result of each get operation performed.
example_input:
2
put 1 1
put 2 2
get 1
put 3 3
get 2
put 4 4
get 1
get 3
get 4

title: Valid Anagram
problem_statement: Given two strings s and t, determine if t is an anagram of s (i.e., contains the same characters with the same frequencies, possibly in a different order).
input_format: First line contains string s. Second line contains string t.
output_format: Print 'true' if t is an anagram of s, otherwise 'false'.

title: Valid Palindrome
problem_statement: Given a string, determine if it is a palindrome, considering only alphanumeric characters and ignoring case.
input_format: A single line containing the string.
output_format: Print 'true' if it is a valid palindrome, otherwise 'false'.
example_input: A man, a plan, a canal: Panama

title: Reverse String
problem_statement: Given a string, reverse it in-place using O(1) extra space.
input_format: A single line containing the string.
output_format: Print the reversed string.

title: Reverse Words
problem_statement: Given a string containing words separated by spaces, reverse the order of the words while removing any leading, trailing, or extra spaces between words.
input_format: A single line containing the string.
output_format: Print the string with word order reversed.

title: Longest Common Prefix
problem_statement: Given an array of strings, find the longest common prefix string among all the strings in the array. If there is no common prefix, return an empty string.
input_format: First line contains N. Second line contains N space separated strings.
output_format: Print the longest common prefix.

title: Roman to Integer
problem_statement: Given a roman numeral string, convert it to an integer.
input_format: A single line containing a valid roman numeral.
output_format: Print the integer value.

title: Integer to Roman
problem_statement: Given an integer, convert it to a roman numeral string.
input_format: A single line containing an integer.
output_format: Print the roman numeral representation.

title: String Compression
problem_statement: Given an array of characters, compress it in-place by replacing consecutive repeating characters with the character followed by the count (counts of 1 are not written), and return the new length.
input_format: A single line containing the character array as a string.
output_format: Print the compressed string and its new length.

title: Longest Substring Without Repeating Characters
problem_statement: Given a string, find the length of the longest substring without repeating characters.
input_format: A single line containing the string.
output_format: Print the length of the longest substring without repeating characters.

title: Group Anagrams
problem_statement: Given an array of strings, group the anagrams together. You may return the answer in any order.
input_format: First line contains N. Second line contains N space separated strings.
output_format: Print the groups of anagrams, one group per line.
example_input:
6
eat tea tan ate nat bat
example_output:
eat tea ate
tan nat
bat

title: Minimum Window Substring
problem_statement: Given two strings s and t, find the minimum window substring of s such that every character in t (including duplicates) is included in the window. Return an empty string if no such substring exists.
input_format: First line contains string s. Second line contains string t.
output_format: Print the minimum window substring.

title: Decode String
problem_statement: Given an encoded string in the form k[encoded_string], decode it fully, where encoded_string is repeated k times.
input_format: A single line containing the encoded string.
output_format: Print the decoded string.

title: Zigzag Conversion
problem_statement: Given a string and a number of rows, write the string in a zigzag pattern across the given number of rows, then read line by line to produce the output string.
input_format: First line contains the string. Second line contains numRows.
output_format: Print the zigzag converted string.

title: Count and Say
problem_statement: The count-and-say sequence is defined by starting with '1', where each term is generated by describing the previous term (run-length encoding). Given n, return the nth term of the sequence.
input_format: A single line containing n.
output_format: Print the nth term of the count-and-say sequence.

title: Compare Version Numbers
problem_statement: Given two version numbers, version1 and version2, compare them. Return -1 if version1 < version2, 1 if version1 > version2, and 0 if they are equal.
input_format: First line contains version1. Second line contains version2.
output_format: Print -1, 0, or 1 based on the comparison.

title: Multiply Strings
problem_statement: Given two non-negative integers represented as strings, return the product of the two numbers, also represented as a string, without using built-in big integer libraries.
input_format: First line contains num1. Second line contains num2.
output_format: Print the product as a string.

title: Implement strStr
problem_statement: Given two strings haystack and needle, return the index of the first occurrence of needle in haystack, or -1 if needle is not part of haystack.
input_format: First line contains haystack. Second line contains needle.
output_format: Print the index of the first occurrence, or -1.

title: KMP Pattern Matching
problem_statement: Given a text string and a pattern string, find all starting indices of the pattern's occurrences in the text using the Knuth-Morris-Pratt algorithm in O(n + m) time.
input_format: First line contains the text. Second line contains the pattern.
output_format: Print all starting indices where the pattern occurs.

title: Rabin-Karp
problem_statement: Given a text string and a pattern string, find all occurrences of the pattern in the text using the Rabin-Karp rolling hash algorithm.
input_format: First line contains the text. Second line contains the pattern.
output_format: Print all starting indices where the pattern occurs.

title: Z Algorithm
problem_statement: Given a string, compute the Z-array where Z[i] is the length of the longest substring starting at i that is also a prefix of the string. Use this to solve pattern matching in O(n + m).
input_format: A single line containing the string (pattern + special separator + text).
output_format: Print the Z-array values.

title: Longest Palindromic Substring
problem_statement: Given a string, find the longest substring that is a palindrome.
input_format: A single line containing the string.
output_format: Print the longest palindromic substring.

title: Shortest Palindrome
problem_statement: Given a string s, convert it to a palindrome by adding characters only in front of it, and return the shortest such palindrome.
input_format: A single line containing the string.
output_format: Print the shortest palindrome that can be formed.

title: Text Justification
problem_statement: Given an array of words and a maximum width, format the text such that each line has exactly maxWidth characters, fully justified with extra spaces distributed as evenly as possible.
input_format: First line contains N and maxWidth. Second line contains N space separated words.
output_format: Print the fully justified lines.

title: Reverse Vowels
problem_statement: Given a string, reverse only the vowels in the string, keeping the rest of the characters in their original positions.
input_format: A single line containing the string.
output_format: Print the string with vowels reversed.

title: Isomorphic Strings
problem_statement: Given two strings s and t, determine if they are isomorphic, meaning the characters in s can be replaced to get t, with a consistent one-to-one mapping.
input_format: First line contains s. Second line contains t.
output_format: Print 'true' if isomorphic, otherwise 'false'.

title: Word Pattern
problem_statement: Given a pattern string and a string consisting of words separated by spaces, determine if the string follows the same pattern, with a full one-to-one mapping between letters and words.
input_format: First line contains the pattern. Second line contains the string of words.
output_format: Print 'true' if it follows the pattern, otherwise 'false'.

title: Add Binary
problem_statement: Given two binary strings, return their sum, also as a binary string.
input_format: First line contains binary string a. Second line contains binary string b.
output_format: Print the binary sum.

title: Valid Parentheses String
problem_statement: Given a string containing only the characters '(', ')' and '*' (where '*' can represent '(', ')', or an empty string), determine if the string is valid, meaning the parentheses can be matched correctly.
input_format: A single line containing the string.
output_format: Print 'true' if the string is valid, otherwise 'false'.

title: Custom String Sort
problem_statement: Given a string 'order' representing a custom character ordering and another string s, sort the characters of s according to the custom order. Characters not in order can appear at the end in any order.
input_format: First line contains order. Second line contains s.
output_format: Print s sorted according to the custom order.

title: String Rotation
problem_statement: Given two strings s1 and s2, determine if s2 is a rotation of s1 using only one call to a substring-search function.
input_format: First line contains s1. Second line contains s2.
output_format: Print 'true' if s2 is a rotation of s1, otherwise 'false'.

title: Reverse Linked List
problem_statement: Given the head of a singly linked list, reverse the list and return the new head.
input_format: First line contains N. Second line contains N integers representing the list nodes.
output_format: Print the reversed linked list.

title: Middle of Linked List
problem_statement: Given the head of a singly linked list, return the middle node. If there are two middle nodes, return the second one.
input_format: First line contains N. Second line contains N integers representing the list nodes.
output_format: Print the value of the middle node.

title: Merge Two Sorted Lists
problem_statement: Given the heads of two sorted linked lists, merge them into a single sorted linked list and return its head.
input_format: First line contains N and M. Second and third lines contain N and M sorted integers respectively.
output_format: Print the merged sorted linked list.

title: Remove Nth Node
problem_statement: Given the head of a linked list, remove the nth node from the end of the list and return its head.
input_format: First line contains N (list size) and n (node to remove from end). Second line contains N integers.
output_format: Print the list after removing the nth node from the end.

title: Detect Cycle
problem_statement: Given the head of a linked list, determine if the linked list has a cycle in it, using Floyd's cycle detection algorithm.
input_format: First line contains N and pos (index where tail connects, -1 if no cycle). Second line contains N integers.
output_format: Print 'true' if a cycle exists, otherwise 'false'.

title: Linked List Cycle II
problem_statement: Given the head of a linked list, return the node where the cycle begins. If there is no cycle, return null.
input_format: First line contains N and pos (index where tail connects, -1 if no cycle). Second line contains N integers.
output_format: Print the value of the node where the cycle begins, or -1 if none.

title: Intersection of Two Lists
problem_statement: Given the heads of two singly linked lists, find the node at which the two lists intersect, or return null if they do not intersect.
input_format: First line contains the two lists and the intersection point details.

title: Palindrome Linked List
